I've never dived before. Where do I start?

The Try Dive. One full day, two students per instructor, and no certification needed — you'll breathe underwater for the first time in the calm, current-free water at Koh Ma. If you love it, the Basic Diver and Open Water course pick up from exactly where you finished.
How old do you have to be to dive?
8 years old for the Try Dive, and 10 for the Basic Diver and the SSI Open Water course. Children who are too young to dive can snorkel at Sail Rock from the same boat.
Can we come as a family, or with children?

Yes, and plenty do. Non-divers can join the boat and snorkel at Sail Rock for 1,500฿ while the rest of the group dives. Message us on WhatsApp with your group's ages and experience and we'll put together a plan that keeps everybody happy on the same boat.
Will I see a whale shark?

Honestly, maybe — and that is part of the magic. Sail Rock is one of the best places in the Gulf of Thailand to meet them. The textbook season is April to June, but we have had great encounters in February and September too: they are wild animals on their own schedule. What you will reliably see are big schools of barracuda, batfish and trevally around the pinnacle.
When is the best time to dive Koh Phangan?

We dive all year and the water stays at 28–30°C. Sail Rock is at its clearest from about May to October, often 20–30 m of visibility. From January to April the water carries more plankton, so visibility there is closer to 5–10 m — but that plankton is what feeds the huge schools and draws in the whale sharks, and it is when Koh Ma and Little Sail Rock are at their clearest. The only real pause is the monsoon, roughly November to mid-December, when we close on days the boats can't safely go out.
How do I get to the shop? Do you pick up from hotels?

The shop is in Chaloklum village, on the north coast of Koh Phangan, and the boat leaves from Chaloklum pier. We don't run hotel pick-ups: taxis on the island are expensive, and renting a scooter for the day (around 250฿) is cheaper and easier. Open the map above for directions.
How do I book and pay?

Message us on WhatsApp with your dates and level. A deposit secures your place, and you can pay in cash or by Revolut. Drop by the shop the day before to fill in the registration forms, then meet us at the boat on Chaloklum pier at 9:15. If we cancel the boat because of the weather, you get a full refund.
What do I need to bring?

A swimsuit, a towel and sun protection. All diving equipment is included — regulators, BCDs and wetsuits in XS to XXL, all new as of 2024 and checked daily. A hot lunch with rice between dives, plenty of fruit and hot and cold drinks are included too. Want a video? Rent an underwater camera for 600฿, or have your instructor film your dive for 800฿.
Which languages do you teach in?

Our instructors teach in English, Spanish and French. For much of the season we also have an instructor who speaks Italian and German, and Russian on some dates — ask when you book. Rui, who runs the office, speaks English and Chinese.

When is the best time to dive Sail Rock?

Sail Rock can be dived all year. It is at its clearest from about May to October, often with 20–30 m of visibility. From January to April the water carries more plankton and visibility is closer to 5–10 m — but that plankton feeds the huge schools of fish and draws in the whale sharks, so it is a different kind of good.
When is visibility best at Koh Ma and Little Sail Rock?

From January to around May or June. The closer sites are at their clearest just when Sail Rock is at its most plankton-rich, which is one of the reasons we choose the route each morning from the conditions.
When is whale shark season at Sail Rock?
The textbook season is April to June, but whale sharks keep their own calendar: we have had great encounters in February and September too. Nobody can promise one, and that is part of the magic.

How much is the SSI Open Water course in Koh Phangan?

12,900฿ per person. That includes your SSI instructor, the digital learning, all the equipment, the boat days with lunch and drinks, and your certification. The only optional extra is an underwater camera (600฿ rental) or a video of your dives filmed by your instructor (800฿).
How long does the Open Water course take?
Three days. Before the first day, you can read the theory online at your own pace, which leaves more time in the water.
Yes. SSI and PADI both train to the same international standards, and an SSI Open Water Diver certification is accepted at dive centres all over the world — including PADI centres.
Do I need to be a strong swimmer?
No. You need to be comfortable in the water: able to swim a short distance without stopping and float for a few minutes. Speed does not matter, and we check it together on the first day.
Can children do the Open Water course?
Yes, from 10 years old. Divers aged 10 to 14 certify as SSI Junior Open Water Divers, with some depth limits until they turn 15, when the card upgrades to the full Open Water Diver.
What if I'm nervous or not sure I will like it?

Start with a Try Dive: one day, no certification needed. If you enjoy it, tell us and we will explain how to continue into the Open Water course. Nervous students are normal, and small groups of four give us time for everyone.
Where do the training dives take place?

The first skills are practised in Chaloklum Bay, in shallow water off the beach. We prefer the sea to a pool: salt water feels different from fresh water, and the beach gives more space and a first short dive. The open-water dives on days two and three are at Sail Rock, an open-sea pinnacle about an hour by boat. When the sea or the students need it, we go to Koh Ma instead, a calmer, shallower coral garden ten minutes from the pier.

Swimwear, a towel, sun protection and something warm for the boat ride home. All the diving equipment is on the boat in your size. If you wear glasses and need a prescription mask, tell us before you arrive.
When can I fly after the course?

The usual guideline is 12 hours after a single shallow dive, 18 hours after several dives or a deep dive, and 24 hours after a decompression dive. The course has several dives a day, so plan on 18 hours. The ferry needs no wait: we are back at the pier around 15:30, in time for a 17:00 ferry.

A granite pinnacle alone in the open sea between Koh Phangan and Koh Tao, rising from 40 metres to above the surface. Schools of barracuda and batfish, a swim-through called The Chimney and, some days, a whale shark. This is what to expect, when to go and how to dive it.

Sail Rock — Hin Bai in Thai — stands alone in open water, far from any reef. With nowhere else to shelter, the fish of the open sea gather around it: that is why it is the best dive site in the Gulf and the one almost every diver on Koh Phangan and Koh Tao wants to see.

The rock drops away on all sides, so there is a depth for every level: new divers stay on the upper walls, certified divers circle the pinnacle deeper, and Deep divers can reach the sandy bottom at 40 metres.

Sail Rock's signature feature is a vertical tunnel through the middle of the pinnacle. The top opening is at 6 metres, the bottom one at 18 metres, and halfway down a window in the wall opens out between 10 and 14 metres.

It can be swum from the top down, from the bottom up, or entered and left through the window. We prefer top to bottom: going down avoids any uncontrolled ascent. No special course is needed — unlike a cave, it is open to the surface above, so in an emergency you can always go straight up. Your guide decides on the day, depending on your level.

Will I see a whale shark at Sail Rock?
Nobody can promise one. The textbook season is April to June, and we have also had great encounters in February and September. When one comes through, it is the dive of a lifetime.

Is there current at Sail Rock?

Sometimes. Because it stands in open sea, the current changes from day to day, but it usually hits only one side of the rock. We plan every dive to avoid it and brief you on the boat before you get in.
Is it better to dive Sail Rock from Koh Phangan or Koh Tao?
Both islands run trips there. From Chaloklum it is about an hour by boat, and with our 9:30 departure we usually arrive as the early boats are leaving, so the rock is quieter.

Despite the name, the whale shark is a fish — the largest fish alive. It feeds by filtering plankton and tiny fish from the water, has no interest in people, and moves slowly enough that you can swim alongside it for a while.
Every whale shark has its own pattern of white spots, as unique as a fingerprint. The species is listed as endangered, which is one more reason to treat every encounter with respect.

Whale sharks follow the plankton. From January to April the water around Sail Rock is full of it, the big schools of fish feed on it, and the whale sharks come in behind them. But they keep their own calendar.

Whale sharks feed near the surface as often as in the depths, so you do not need to be an experienced diver. The more days you spend at Sail Rock, the better your chances.

When is whale shark season in Koh Phangan?

The textbook season at Sail Rock is April to June. Whale sharks keep their own calendar, though: we have had great encounters in February and September too, and a sighting is possible at other times of the year.
Where can I see whale sharks near Koh Phangan?
At Sail Rock, the open-sea pinnacle between Koh Phangan and Koh Tao. It is the best place in this part of the Gulf of Thailand to meet them, and about an hour by boat from Chaloklum.
Is a whale shark sighting guaranteed?

No, and the chance on any single day is low. Nobody feeds or attracts whale sharks here: they come and go naturally with the plankton, which is what makes every encounter so special. Diving Sail Rock on several days during the season is the best way to improve your chances.
No. Whale sharks feed on plankton and small fish and are harmless to people. The only real risk is to the whale shark, which is why we ask everyone to keep their distance and never touch it.
Can I see a whale shark without diving?
Yes. Whale sharks often feed near the surface, and some of the most spectacular sightings we have had were while snorkelling. Snorkellers can join our boat to Sail Rock for 1,500฿.
Do I need to be an experienced diver?

No. Whale sharks swim at every depth and often near the surface, so Open Water students and snorkellers have as good a chance as experienced divers. What matters is being in the water on the right day.
Will I get photos of the whale shark?
Rent an underwater camera for 600฿ or have your instructor film your dive for 800฿, and if a whale shark comes through, you take it home with you. Please remember: no flash.

What is Nitrox and why use it?

Nitrox, or enriched air, has more oxygen and less nitrogen than normal air. It does not let you dive deeper; in fact the course teaches you the maximum depth for each mix.

The questions we are asked every week on the boat: when can I fly, can I dive with a cold, is diabetes a problem, what does decompression sickness feel like? Here are clear answers, based on the guidelines of Divers Alert Network (DAN).
Feeling OK is the first rule
Every diver fills in a short medical questionnaire. Answer it honestly: some conditions only need a doctor's signature before you dive, and it is much better to know that before the boat leaves.
A cold or blocked nose: wait until it clears — you will not be able to equalise
Equalise early and often on the way down, and never force it
Drink plenty of water; heat and sun dehydrate you fast
No alcohol the night before — Full Moon Party included
Pregnant? Do not dive; come snorkelling with us instead
Asthma, heart conditions, epilepsy or recent surgery: talk to a doctor first

After diving your body still holds extra nitrogen, and the lower pressure in a plane cabin can turn it into decompression sickness. DAN recommends these minimum surface intervals — longer is always better.
Wait at least 12 hours before flying.
Wait at least 18 hours. This is the one that applies to a normal two-dive day and to every course.
Taking the ferry is fine: you are back at Chaloklum pier around 15:30, in time for a 17:00 ferry. Just plan your last dive day around your flight from Koh Samui, Surat Thani or Bangkok.

Decompression sickness (DCS) is rare in recreational diving, and slow ascents, safety stops and staying within your computer's limits make it rarer still. But every diver should recognise it, because early oxygen and treatment make a real difference.
Unusual tiredness or feeling generally unwell
Difficulty walking or loss of coordination
Confusion, dizziness or a spinning sensation
Ringing in the ears or hearing loss
If you notice any of these after diving, do not fly and do not wait to see if it passes: tell us, get medical help straight away, and call DAN's 24-hour emergency hotline on
Many people with diabetes dive safely. DAN's guidelines set out who can dive and how to manage blood glucose on a dive day. Talk to your doctor, and tell us and your buddy before the dive.
HbA1c of 9% or less, in good overall health
Under medical supervision, with no new medication
No history of unnoticed hypos, or hypos that needed someone else's help
Test 60, 30 and 0 minutes before the dive
Enter the water at 150 mg/dL (8.3 mmol/L) or more, stable or rising
Delay the dive below 150 or above 300 mg/dL (16.7 mmol/L)
Carry fast glucose, and keep checking for 12–15 hours after diving
Dives deeper than 30 m or longer than 60 minutes
A buddy who is also diabetic
If you feel any symptoms during a dive, signal your buddy, end the dive, surface and get checked.
Almost nothing in the Gulf of Thailand is dangerous if you keep your hands to yourself and your fins off the bottom. A few animals deserve extra respect.
Their stings are very painful and can be serious. If stung, get out of the water, pour vinegar over the area for at least 30 seconds, do not rub it, and get medical help.
Masters of camouflage with venomous spines. Never put a hand or knee down without looking. A sting needs hot water — as hot as you can bear — and a doctor.
Sea urchin spines, fire coral and some anemones sting or cut. Good buoyancy is the best protection — for you and for the reef.
How long should I wait to fly after diving?

DAN recommends at least 12 hours after a single no-decompression dive, 18 hours after repetitive dives or several days of diving, and 24 hours after a decompression dive. For a normal two-dive day or a course, plan on 18 hours.
Can I dive with a cold?

Better not. A blocked nose or sinuses make it hard or impossible to equalise, which can damage your ears. Decongestants can wear off during the dive. Wait until you can breathe clearly through your nose.

Often, yes. DAN's guidelines allow adults with well-controlled diabetes to dive with careful glucose checks before and after each dive, and some limits on depth and dive time. Talk to your doctor and tell us before you book.
Can I dive the day after the Full Moon Party?
Alcohol and dehydration raise the risk of decompression sickness and make you less alert. If you have been drinking heavily the night before, move your dive by a day — we will happily change it.
What are the symptoms of decompression sickness?

Mild signs include joint or muscle pain, skin rash or mottling and unusual tiredness. Serious signs include numbness, tingling or weakness, difficulty walking, confusion, dizziness, chest pain or breathing difficulty, and hearing problems. With any of them, do not fly, get medical help and call DAN.
Can I dive if I am pregnant?
No. Diving is not recommended at any stage of pregnancy. You are very welcome on the boat to snorkel at Sail Rock instead.
Sometimes. It depends on how well controlled it is and what triggers it, so you need a doctor to assess you and sign the medical form before diving.

What marine life can you see at Sail Rock?

Mostly big schools: bigeye trevally, barracuda and batfish around the pinnacle, with hunters like Spanish mackerel passing through. On the walls there are morays, filefish, Christmas tree worms and nudibranchs, and from time to time a whale shark.
What can you see at Koh Ma?
A shallow hard-coral garden with green turtles, clownfish in their anemones, boxfish and bannerfish, and cuttlefish and soles on the sand around the reef.
Are there sharks around Koh Phangan?
Yes, but nothing to worry about. The ones divers meet are whale sharks, which feed on plankton, and leopard sharks, which rest calmly on the sand. Both are harmless to people.

Very little, as long as you do not touch anything. Scorpionfish and stonefish have venomous spines, sea urchins and fire coral sting, and box jellyfish can appear near the surface. Our health and safety page explains what to do.

Koh Phangan or Koh Tao FAQ
Is diving better on Koh Tao or Koh Phangan?

The best dive site in the area, Sail Rock, is shared by both islands. Koh Tao has more sites close to shore and many more dive shops; Koh Phangan is quieter, with smaller groups and a more personal feel. Neither is better — they suit different people.
Is it cheaper to learn to dive on Koh Tao?
Usually, yes. With around 80 dive centres competing, prices on Koh Tao are some of the lowest you will find. On Koh Phangan you pay a little more for smaller groups and more personal attention.
How many dive shops are there on each island?
Around 80 on Koh Tao and around 15 on Koh Phangan, which is a much bigger island.
Which island is closer to Sail Rock?
From Chaloklum, on the north coast of Koh Phangan, it takes about an hour. From Koh Tao it takes around half an hour longer, and not every shop goes there every day.
Is Koh Phangan only about the Full Moon Party?
No. The big parties are in the south of the island. The north, where Chaloklum is, is quiet and family-friendly, and you would not notice the parties at all.
Can I dive Sail Rock from both islands?
Yes. It is equally busy whichever island the boats come from. We leave Chaloklum about an hour and a quarter after the other boats, so we usually have the second dive to ourselves.

Best Time to Dive in Koh Phangan — Month by Month at Sail Rock and Koh Ma
You can dive here almost every month of the year. The real question is what you want to see: the clearest water, a whale shark, or calm conditions for your first dives.

Koh Phangan sits on the Gulf of Thailand side of the country, so its seasons are different from Phuket and the Andaman Sea. There is no long closed season here: we go out every month, and the only real break is the monsoon at the end of the year.

Can you dive in Koh Phangan all year?
Almost. We dive every month of the year. During the monsoon, roughly November to mid-December, the boat stays in on days when the sea is unsafe, and you get a full refund.
When is the visibility best at Sail Rock?

From May to October, often 20 to 30 metres. From January to April there is more plankton in the water and visibility is closer to 5 to 10 metres, but that plankton is what brings the big schools of fish and the whale sharks.
When is the best time to see whale sharks?
April to June is the textbook season, and we have also had great encounters in February and September. A sighting is never guaranteed.
When is the best time to learn to dive in Koh Phangan?

Any month outside the monsoon. The first day of the Open Water course is in the shallow water of Chaloklum Bay, and we choose between Sail Rock and the calmer Koh Ma for the open-water dives depending on the conditions.
